brand.name: The Interested Indian
brand.promise: Why India works the way it does — one exam, city, industry, policy or social contradiction at a time

principles: Original, human-reviewed documentary and explainer work.
Never use a policy term without immediately translating it.
Explain the system, not just the event.
A claim without a source is not a claim.

prohibited: Copying the character or any part of its design

legacy_config._speaking_rate_note: 0.25=slowest, 1.0=default, 4.0=fastest. 'gemini' provider implements this via SSML <prosody rate='85%'>; 'gemini_cloudtts' uses the native audioConfig.speakingRate field instead. Charon at 1.0 felt rushed — 0.85 works well for Iapetus too.
legacy_config.gemini_note: Historical: Charon selected 2026-07-25 for the plain 'gemini' provider — deep, authoritative, tested vs Fenrir/Orus/Puck. Superseded 2026-07-27 by Iapetus for 'gemini_cloudtts' (see _gemini_cloudtts_note) — kept here since 'gemini' provider fallback still defaults to gemini_voice.
legacy_config.gemini_cloudtts_style: Narrate in a predominantly American English accent with only a faint trace of Indian origin - like an Indian-born professional who emigrated to the United States 30 years ago and now sounds mostly American, just a subtle hint of the original accent remaining. Confident, articulate, sophisticated young professional narrator, smooth natural pacing, understated warmth.
legacy_config._gemini_cloudtts_note: Voice: Iapetus. Style updated 2026-07-27 to the 'Indian-American hybrid, more American than Indian' variant — an Indian-born narrator who's lived in the US 30 years, mostly American accent with just a faint Indian trace — see voice_previews/gemini31_Iapetus_enIN_indianamerican_moreus.wav, the one selected (chosen over the plain 'classy Indian English' variant and over the equivalent Charon take). This is a deliberate departure from the earlier 'must say Indian English explicitly' finding below — here the goal is for Indian-ness to be a subtle undertone, not the dominant accent, so the style text says so explicitly rather than omitting it (omitting any Indian-origin mention entirely was NOT tested here and would likely drift to fully generic American, per the earlier finding). IMPORTANT (general, still applies): the style prompt's own wording is what actually shapes the accent — locale=en-IN alone doesn't determine it; confirmed empirically in an earlier A/B that omitting any Indian-accent wording caused full drift away from Indian. Goes through Cloud Text-to-Speech (texttospeech.googleapis.com), a different API from the Gemini Developer API the 'gemini' provider uses — Cloud TTS rejects plain API keys, so this REQUIRES the gcloud CLI installed and authenticated (gcloud auth login) on whatever machine runs the pipeline. Falls back to provider 'gemini' if gcloud isn't available.
legacy_config._speed_note: ElevenLabs generation-time pacing control (0.7-1.2 typical range, baked into synthesis so pitch/timbre stay natural — NOT a post-hoc time-stretch). Set 2026-07-28 after measuring the default-speed Cyber Creed narration at 165.2 WPM (1964 words / 11.89 min), which felt fast for dense explainer content; 0.9 targets roughly 149 WPM. This is a different parameter from gemini_speaking_rate above — that one's Gemini-only.
legacy_config._target_lufs_note: Two-pass ffmpeg loudnorm applied once to the full narration file right after generation (generate_source_audio.py's normalize_loudness()), before the split stage cuts per-scene clips from it — every clip inherits consistent loudness for free instead of each tiny clip being normalized independently (unreliable on short audio). -14 LUFS is the common streaming-platform target. Skipped for --preview (short A/B clips). Real narration measured this pipeline was averaging around -27 LUFS before this existed, with no consistency across TTS provider switches.
legacy_config.elevenlabs_note: COMMENTED OUT / INACTIVE as of 2026-07-29 in favor of 'grok' — see grok_note. This config block is intentionally left in place (not deleted) so switching back to 'elevenlabs' is a one-line provider change if the Grok voice clone doesn't work out. History: switched 2026-07-28 from gemini_cloudtts to elevenlabs — Cloud TTS's per-chunk synthesis caused an audible voice/tone shift at chunk boundaries on long scripts (documented model limitation, no fix available). Voice 'Cyber Creed' (aJm4vjjSZkqTKDkM19X1) chosen after sampling 20 Indian-male candidates from ElevenLabs' shared-voice-library (clear/approachable register, lighter accent — earlier candidates were rejected as too heavy). Model is eleven_multilingual_v2, NOT eleven_turbo_v2_5 — first tried turbo_v2_5 specifically for its 40k-char single-request capacity (avoids chunk seams entirely), but a direct same-voice/same-text A/B confirmed turbo_v2_5 renders this voice audibly differently from multilingual_v2, and multilingual_v2 was the one actually approved after listening. multilingual_v2 caps at 10k chars/request, so our ~12k-char script still needs 2 chunks (1 seam) — an explicit, accepted trade-off: quality/voice-match over the (smaller, 1-seam) residual drift risk. Previously tried 'ANX - Deep & Friendly' (gYQ0co3BoppQZ8BDM3lj) was rejected earlier for sounding generic/not distinctly Indian despite being tagged 'indian' accent in ElevenLabs' own metadata — don't trust the accent tag alone, always listen.
legacy_config._grok_speed_note: Naksh at 0.9 pronounces lakh/crore/MBBS/Indian city names correctly (tested with dedicated pronunciation script). Cosmo at any speed mispronounced lakh as 'lock'. Speed changes re-synthesize, not time-stretch, so pronunciation varies per voice+speed combo.
legacy_config.grok_note: Switched 2026-07-29 from elevenlabs to grok (xAI). Voice is now 'Naksh', one of Grok's built-in voices — switched 2026-07-30 from the earlier custom clone 'giri_1' (voice_id 5zesaz2wahi2, created via console.x.ai's Voice Library) after a live pronunciation test (lakh/crore/MBBS/Indian city names) showed Naksh at speed 0.9 was the most reliable of several candidates tried (Cosmo, Helios, Perseus, giri_1) — see _grok_speed_note. giri_1 is still available in the Voice Library if a custom clone is wanted again later. Reuses XAI_API_KEY already in .env for image generation, no new secret. Pricing ~$15/1M chars, cheaper than ElevenLabs; single request handles up to 15,000 chars (this script is ~11,830, fits in one call — no chunk-seam risk, unlike elevenlabs_default's 2-chunk situation above). IMPORTANT — response format: xAI's own docs page describes a JSON response with a base64 'audio' field, but a real live test call proved that wrong — the API actually returns raw binary MP3 bytes directly (Content-Type: audio/mpeg). Caught immediately via a UnicodeDecodeError when the first implementation tried to JSON-parse the raw bytes; don't trust that docs page's response-shape description if xAI ever changes this again — verify against a real call.
legacy_config.edge_note: Switched 2026-07-31 from grok to edge (free, no API key). Reason: Naksh (grok) pronounced lakh/crore/MBBS/city-names correctly but the accent itself leans American, not Indian — a bigger problem for a channel called 'The Interested Indian' than any pronunciation quirk. edge-tts's en-IN locale has only 3 voices total (NeerjaNeural, NeerjaExpressiveNeural — both female — and PrabhatNeural, the only male one), so there's no alternative en-IN male voice to compare against. Prabhat confirmed via live test: correct lakh/crore/M.B.B.S./city-name pronunciation, genuinely Indian-accented (not a compromise like gemini_cloudtts's deliberate Indian-American hybrid above). rate=+12%/pitch=+15Hz chosen after local A/B against the default and a more/less punchy pass. KNOWN LIMITATION #1, confirmed via a direct A/B against en-US-GuyNeural on the same 5 test sentences: Prabhat does not produce rising intonation on question-mark sentences (flat delivery even on genuine yes-no questions like 'Was he really on the ground?') — en-US-GuyNeural rose correctly on the same text, so this is specific to the en-IN voice model's prosody training, not an edge-tts-wide limitation, and not fixable via rate/pitch. Worked around by rephrasing the script's rhetorical questions as declaratives. edge-tts also has no bracket-tag speech-control system like Grok's [pause]/<soft>/<emphasis> (confirmed working with Naksh) — Azure's engine uses SSML instead, which edge-tts's Python API doesn't expose per-word, only global rate/pitch/volume — so that personability work doesn't carry over to this voice. KNOWN LIMITATION #2, found 2026-07-31 reviewing the first full pilot_neet_scandal render at this voice: 'NEET-UG' (the episode's actual subject) mispronounced 3/3 times in the all-caps hyphenated form (rendered as 'NETUG'/'an ETUG' — confirmed via WhisperX's own transcript of the real audio, not just a caption-text guess). Root-caused via isolated live tests: respelling as 'Neet U.G.' (mixed case) renders correctly — the all-caps hyphenated acronym form seems to confuse Prabhat's text normalizer. Separately, 'Pass' gets substituted with 'Ask' specifically when it's the first word of a sentence (confirmed 3/3 reproducible in isolated tests; 'If you pass it...' mid-sentence rendered correctly) — apply the same sentence-initial-avoidance workaround for any future 'Pass'-led sentence. Both fixes applied to pilot_neet_scandal's script 2026-07-31, but narration/split/images have NOT yet been regenerated against the fixed text as of this commit — see interesting_indian_session.md for pickup point.
legacy_config.note: Provider: 'gemini_cloudtts' (Indian-accented via Cloud TTS + en-IN locale + style prompt, needs gcloud auth, has a documented cross-chunk voice-drift issue on long scripts), 'gemini' (Gemini Developer API, simple API key, no locale/style control), 'elevenlabs' (commented out/inactive — see elevenlabs_note), 'grok' (xAI, correct pronunciation but Naksh's accent leans American — see edge_note), 'edge' (current default — free Microsoft Azure TTS via edge-tts, genuinely Indian-accented; see edge_note for the known question-intonation limitation). Switch provider here or pass --provider flag.
